_meta.note: Canonical video script. Each line is spoken by Kokoro af_heart and shown in the 90 px caption band below the 1920x990 app frame (letterboxed, so captions never cover the UI). 'take' names a scripted Playwright take in scripts/video/takes.py (card:<id> = a still from scripts/video/cards.html). Build: scripts/video/make-draft.sh <out_dir> (FINAL=1 for the final render).
_meta.rules: No greeting; the voice never claims to be a person. No statistic unless verified against a primary source and cited on screen (none is used). No credentials or personal data on screen. Specific names in lines must match the Big Thief preset (takes.py writes facts.json). No placeholder text in a final render.
_meta.endcard: Credit is on-screen text only. Links come from scripts/video/config.json.

lines: Type any act and confirm the match on Qloo. Then it scouts live, one Qloo call at a time.
Here is a captured Big Thief run.
Qloo's fan map lights up where this audience concentrates across the country.
Each hotspot becomes a touring city, scored by how strongly these fans favour its live rooms.
Every city is ranked. The cut line shows why these five made it: a tight New England run.
Each stop shows where fans cluster, real rooms they favour, and an opener whose audience shares their taste.
Claude drafts each booker pitch, citing Qloo evidence.
Ask the scout. An agent picks Qloo tools, runs them, and proposes a change.
The server checks the proposal. Apply it, and Andy Shauf becomes the Burlington opener.
Flip on receipts: every value links to the exact Qloo request behind it. No credentials, no personal data.
It works for stand-up comedians, with comedy clubs and club comics as openers.
And for new acts, planned from the fans of artists they sound like.
Under the hood: the official Qloo harness, and Claude Haiku for the words.
Tour Scout. Find your fans before you book the room. Thanks for watching.
